_comment: How the loose tokens in Items.location resolve.
Concrete place names are handled by the `aliases` list on each record in
vocab/locations.json. This file covers the rest: habitats, tokens to ignore,
and fragments that are not locations at all.
THE HABITAT DECISION, as settled at D4. The wiki says 'Pond'. There are three
ponds — and the Fishing page names them, along with the four rivers and the
three places the ocean is reachable. So the *set* is a fact and is parsed like
What remains an inference is whether a given fish is in all of them. The
expanded window carries `confidence: 'inferred'` and the UI draws those pins
hollow. It is not also a `locations` data gap: the two would be recording the
same uncertainty twice, and a gap that can never be closed is noise.
The expansion list is NOT hand-typed here. It comes from the source, so a
region added to the wiki appears without anyone editing this file. What lives
here is only whether a habitat is expandable at all.

_policy_note: 'Overworld' means outdoors with no particular place in mind, so there is
nothing to expand it into. Nine pins on nine regions would turn an
absence of information into nine confident claims. It stays a habitat,
and the item keeps its `locations` data gap.

_ignore_comment: Tokens that carry no location information. 'Any' and 'Any Floor Without a Seal'
are real values but say nothing a pin could use; they become a data gap rather
'Archaeology' and 'Mining' are skill names that leaked into the location column
on the wiki. They are recorded here so they don't sit in the unresolved queue
forever pretending to be a curation to-do.
ignore: No set spawn area, rarely spawn anywhere in the overworld.
_pattern_comment: Fragments produced when the wiki splits a cell across lines. A floor range is a
depth constraint on the window, not a place, and 'Dig Spots (requires Well
Placed Skill)' is a spawn method plus a perk gate.
Anything matching these is consumed by the resolver rather than reported as an
